column3: The Hebrew does not explicitly introduce a time phrase, as BSB does with “About that time.” It calls the other Jews their brothers; BSB says fellow Jews.

The Hebrew compares their flesh with their brothers’ flesh and describes the absence of power in their hand; BSB speaks of being like their countrymen and being powerless. BSB explicitly supplies redeeming them.
The Hebrew pictures his heart taking counsel within him; BSB says “after serious thought.”
The Hebrew says they found no word; BSB says they could find nothing to say.
The Hebrew specifies a hundredth of the money and produce; BSB says “the percentage.”
The Hebrew says he made “them” swear without naming them again; BSB specifies the nobles and officials.
The Hebrew names the man’s toil; BSB says possession. It describes him as emptied; BSB says he would have nothing.
The Hebrew leaves the initial appointing subject unnamed; BSB explicitly names King Artaxerxes at that point.
The Hebrew says a field in the singular; BSB says any land.
The Hebrew says those coming to us from the nations; BSB calls them guests.
The Hebrew says the governor’s bread and describes the service as heavy upon the people; BSB says allotted food and a heavy burden.
